guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are less pessimistic about Purdue than the market, and the offense offers some reason for that difference. We are not treating the Indiana State opener as proof, but Ryan Browne is a returning starter with 15 career starts for Purdue, and he completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns in that game. That continuity at quarterback matters to us when the market is asking Purdue to stay competitive on the road.

The concern is that Purdue remains difficult to evaluate around Browne. Sixteen players made their first Purdue starts in the opener, including six offensive linemen, while our longer-run metrics show UCLA with potential advantages in the running game and in creating scoring opportunities. We can see a path for Purdue to remain within range, but its passing profile against UCLA's defense is not strong enough to make the modest disagreement actionable. For us, the available price does not provide enough value, so this remains a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching UCLA's rushing offense against Purdue's run defense. Our matchup numbers identify this as UCLA's clearest route to sustained offense, particularly because Purdue's broader scoring-opportunity prevention also grades poorly. Purdue held Indiana State to 66 rushing yards, but we view that as one encouraging result rather than evidence that the longer-run concern has disappeared. If UCLA consistently creates favorable down-and-distance situations on the ground, Purdue will have a harder time keeping the game inside the market's expectation.

guide_extractions.document_match_reason: This is Purdue's Game 2 guide for the Sept. 12, 2026 matchup against Wake Forest, not the Week 3 game at UCLA on Sept. 19. It contains limited advance information about the UCLA game plus current Purdue personnel and season-opening performance information.

recent_game.fact: Purdue opened the 2026 season with a 44-19 home victory over Indiana State.
Purdue produced 523 total yards against Indiana State, its first 500-yard game since Oct. 12, 2024 at Illinois.
Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana State.
Fame Ijeboi led Purdue with 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and added two receptions for 30 yards against Indiana State.
Asaad Waseem caught six passes for 107 yards and one touchdown in his Purdue debut against Indiana State.
Purdue held Indiana State to 284 total yards, including 66 rushing yards, and 12 first downs.
Purdue committed no turnovers, gained one takeaway and held the ball for 37:22 against Indiana State.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue is scheduled to play UCLA at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena on Sept. 19, 2026, with an 11 p.m. ET kickoff on BTN.
The 11 p.m. ET kickoff against UCLA would be Purdue's latest start since an 11:05 p.m. ET game at Hawaii on Nov. 25, 2006.
The UCLA game will be Purdue's third game at the Rose Bowl stadium; its previous appearances there were Rose Bowl Games against USC in 1967 and Washington in 2001.
The Rose Bowl is listed as 2,086 miles from Purdue's Ross-Ade Stadium.

quarterback.fact: Ryan Browne is Purdue's returning starting quarterback and has started 15 career games for the Boilermakers.
Browne started all 12 games in 2025 and passed for 2,153 yards and nine touchdowns.
Browne's 317-yard opener was his fourth career 300-yard passing game.
Evans Chuba and Bennett Meredith competed for the backup quarterback role during the spring and summer; Meredith started at Northwestern in 2023 but did not play in the following two seasons.

offensive_personnel.fact: Sixteen players made their first Purdue starts against Indiana State, including offensive linemen Jackson Berryman, Micah Banuelos, Brock Brownfield, Nuku Mafi, Jude McCoskey and Boaz Stanley.
Brock Brownfield became Purdue's first true freshman offensive lineman to start a season opener since freshmen became eligible in 1972.
Joey Tanona is the only returning Purdue offensive lineman who started all 12 games in 2025; Ethan Trent made six starts and Jude McCoskey played in 11 games.
Purdue added offensive line transfers Boaz Stanley, Nuku Mafi and Micah Banuelos; entering 2026 they had 21, 12 and five career starts, respectively.
The running back room changed after Devin Mockobee's graduation, with Antonio Harris the lone returning running back from 2025.
Minnesota transfer Fame Ijeboi and FAU transfer Asaad Waseem led Purdue in rushing and receiving, respectively, in the season opener.
Xavier Townsend debuted for Purdue with seven catches for 47 yards and three punt returns for 24 yards against Indiana State.

defensive_personnel.fact: Purdue's season-opening defensive starters included newcomers Curt Neal, Keyshawn Burgos, Jojo Hayden, Jaden Mangham, Don Saunders and John Slaughter.
Linebacker Charles Correa returned after recording 96 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks in 12 starts during 2025.
FIU transfer Mister Clark led Purdue against Indiana State with five solo tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass breakup.
Transfer defensive back Don Saunders returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown against Indiana State, Purdue's first pick-six since 2022.
Purdue added defensive line transfers Rodney Lora, Curt Neal and Wisdom Simms, who brought a combined 81 games of college experience, including 60 at the Power Four level.

coaching_changes.fact: Kevin Kane returned to Purdue as defensive coordinator and linebackers coach after serving as a Minnesota defensive analyst in 2025; he previously coordinated Purdue's defense in 2023 and 2024.
Zach Crabtree became Purdue's offensive line coach after coaching at Fresno State in 2025.
Cornell Ford moved from wide receivers coach to running backs coach for 2026.
Bilal Marshall was promoted from offensive analyst to wide receivers coach during the offseason.
Charles Clark joined Purdue as defensive pass game coordinator and defensive backs coach after five seasons at Memphis.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Kylan Fox suffered an injury at the start of training camp and is expected to miss the 2026 season.
Wide receivers De'Nylon Morrissette and Chauncey Magwood returned after missing the 2025 season with injuries.
Magwood played in the 2026 opener and caught a six-yard touchdown, his first touchdown since 2022.
Tight end George Burhenn returned to game action for the first time in 349 days and caught two passes for 43 yards against Indiana State.

offensive_context.fact: Purdue passed for 346 yards and rushed for 177 yards in the season opener.
Purdue converted 54.5 percent of its third downs and scored on every red-zone possession against Indiana State.
Five different Boilermakers scored their first Purdue touchdowns against Indiana State: Tra'Mar Harris, Fame Ijeboi, Chauncey Magwood, Don Saunders and Asaad Waseem.
Purdue added 32 transfers and 22 freshmen for 2026, including 19 transfers from Power Four programs.

defensive_context.fact: Purdue recorded three sacks and eight tackles for loss against Indiana State.
Indiana State converted one of three fourth-down attempts and scored on every red-zone trip against Purdue.
Purdue allowed 218 passing yards and 66 rushing yards in the opener.

special_teams.fact: True freshman kicker Jacobo Echeverria Lozano made all three field-goal attempts and all five extra-point attempts against Indiana State, with a long field goal of 39 yards.
Dylan Drennan punted once for 54 yards with a 49-yard net in the opener.
Drennan transferred from Buffalo after averaging 44.8 yards per punt as a freshman, with 25 punts inside the 20 and 16 punts of at least 50 yards.

series_context.fact: UCLA leads the series with Purdue 3-0-2 and has won the last two meetings.
Purdue previously played UCLA twice in Southern California, tying 0-0 in 1959 and losing 31-21 in 1979; both games were at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.
The 2026 game will be Barry Odom's first meeting with UCLA as a head coach.

other_relevant.fact: Barry Odom is in his second season as Purdue's head coach.
Purdue named Ryan Browne, Charles Correa, Hudauri Hines, Jude McCoskey, De'Nylon Morrissette and Curt Neal as its six 2026 team captains.
Thirty-eight players made their Purdue debuts in the 2026 season opener.
